terms264.name: program
terms264.meaning: A set of instructions for a computer to follow.
terms264.example: A program can add two prices and show the total.

terms264.name: code
terms264.meaning: Instructions written in a programming language.
terms264.example: Code can tell a computer to display a greeting. Each language has its own spelling for that instruction.

terms264.name: value
terms264.meaning: One piece of information that code can use.
terms264.example: 5 is a number value. "Hello" is a text value.

terms264.name: variable
terms264.meaning: A name that lets your code use a value.
terms264.example: A variable named score can hold 5, then be updated to hold 8.

terms264.name: string
terms264.meaning: Text stored as a value. Quotes mark where the text starts and ends.
terms264.example: "Hello" is a string. 5 is a number, but "5" is text.

terms264.name: integer
terms264.meaning: A number with no fractional part. It can be negative, zero, or positive.
terms264.example: 3, 0, and -2 are integers. 3.5 is not.

terms264.name: floating-point number
terms264.meaning: A number type that can hold a fractional part. Some values are only approximate.
terms264.example: A price like 2.5 can be stored as a floating-point number.

terms264.name: Boolean
terms264.meaning: A value with just two choices: true or false.
terms264.example: The question “Is 5 greater than 3?” has the Boolean answer true.

terms264.name: function
terms264.meaning: A reusable block of code that can receive inputs, perform a task, and give back a result. Functions can have names or be unnamed.
terms264.example: A function can add two numbers each time the program asks it to run.

terms264.name: function call
terms264.meaning: An instruction that asks a function to run.
terms264.example: Calling a greeting function asks it to produce a greeting now.

terms264.name: parameter
terms264.meaning: A name in a function definition that stands for an input.
terms264.example: A greeting function can define a parameter named name for the person to greet.

terms264.name: argument
terms264.meaning: A value you give a function when you call it.
terms264.example: Supplying the name Mina to a greeting function passes Mina as its argument.

terms264.name: return value
terms264.meaning: The result a function gives back to the code that called it.
terms264.example: A function that adds 2 and 3 can return 5. Returning is not the same as printing.

terms264.name: method
terms264.meaning: A function that belongs to an object or type.
terms264.example: A text value can have a method that produces uppercase text; its name depends on the language.

terms264.name: expression
terms264.meaning: Code that produces a value.
terms264.example: 2 + 3 is an expression. Its value is 5.

terms264.name: statement
terms264.meaning: An instruction that tells the program to do something.
terms264.example: An assignment statement can store a new value in a score variable.

terms264.name: assignment
terms264.meaning: Giving a value to a name or another place that stores it.
terms264.example: Assigning 5 to score stores that value; it does not ask whether two values are equal.

terms264.name: operator
terms264.meaning: A symbol or word that performs an action on values.
terms264.example: + adds numbers. > compares them.

terms264.name: comparison
terms264.meaning: A check of how values relate, such as whether they are equal.
terms264.example: 5 > 3 compares two numbers and gives true.

terms264.name: condition
terms264.meaning: A check used to decide what happens next.
terms264.example: A condition can ask whether a score is above 10 before choosing what to display.

terms264.name: branch
terms264.meaning: One path a program can take after a decision.
terms264.example: An if branch handles a true condition. An else branch handles the other case.

terms264.name: loop
terms264.meaning: Code that repeats instructions.
terms264.example: A loop can print each name in a list.

terms264.name: iteration
terms264.meaning: One pass through a loop, or the act of going through items.
terms264.example: Printing three list items takes three loop iterations.

terms264.name: list
terms264.meaning: An ordered collection of items.
terms264.example: A shopping list can hold book and pen as two ordered items. Code notation varies by language.

terms264.name: array
terms264.meaning: An ordered collection whose items can be reached by position.
terms264.example: An array can hold 10, 20 and 30 in order. Indexing rules depend on the language.

terms264.name: Collection index
terms264.meaning: A position used to find an item in an ordered collection. Many languages start at 0.
terms264.example: In ["red", "blue"], index 0 selects "red".
terms264.context: Position in a list, array, or similar collection. A database index is a different meaning of index.

terms264.name: Database index
terms264.meaning: An extra database structure that can help find rows faster. It takes space and must be updated when data changes.
terms264.example: An index on genre can speed up a search for books in one genre.
terms264.context: Database lookup structure, not an item’s position in an array.

terms264.name: dictionary
terms264.meaning: A collection that connects keys to values.
terms264.example: A dictionary can connect the key name to the value Mina.

terms264.name: key
terms264.meaning: A label used to find a value in a collection.
terms264.example: The key score can identify a stored value of 5.

terms264.name: tuple
terms264.meaning: An ordered group of values treated as one value. Exact type and mutability rules depend on the language.
terms264.example: A pair of values can represent a point with horizontal and vertical coordinates.

terms264.name: set
terms264.meaning: A Python collection with no duplicate items. It does not provide numbered positions.
terms264.example: {1, 1, 2} creates a set containing 1 and 2.

terms264.name: object
terms264.meaning: A value that can have its own data and actions.
terms264.example: A player object might have a name, a score, and a method to add points.

terms264.name: property
terms264.meaning: A named piece of data or a setting that belongs to something.
terms264.example: A player object can expose a score property.

terms264.name: Class (object-oriented programming)
terms264.meaning: A definition used to create objects with shared kinds of data and behavior.
terms264.example: A Player class can create separate players, each with a score.
terms264.context: A programming type or template for objects. An HTML/CSS class is a different use of the word.

terms264.name: instance
terms264.meaning: One object created from a class or type.
terms264.example: Two Player objects are two separate instances of Player.

terms264.name: mutable
terms264.meaning: Able to be changed after it is made.
terms264.example: A mutable collection can accept another item without replacing the whole collection.

terms264.name: immutable
terms264.meaning: Not changeable after it is made. You can make a new value instead.
terms264.example: An immutable text value cannot be edited in place; an operation can produce a new text value instead.

terms264.name: scope
terms264.meaning: The part of a program where a name can be used.
terms264.example: A local name made inside a function is normally used inside that function.

terms264.name: closure
terms264.meaning: A function that keeps access to names from the place where it was created.
terms264.example: A counter function can remember its count between calls.

terms264.name: recursion
terms264.meaning: Solving a task by having a function call itself on smaller parts.
terms264.example: A folder search can search each folder inside the current folder.

terms264.name: base case
terms264.meaning: The stopping case in a recursive function.
terms264.example: A countdown can stop calling itself when the number reaches 0.

terms264.name: iterator
terms264.meaning: Something that gives you items one at a time and remembers its place.
terms264.example: Asking an iterator for its next item advances through a collection.

terms264.name: iterable
terms264.meaning: Something you can go through item by item.
terms264.example: An iterable collection lets a loop visit its items one by one.

terms264.name: generator
terms264.meaning: Code that produces items one at a time instead of preparing them all at once.
terms264.example: A generator can produce the next number only when it is requested.

terms264.name: syntax
terms264.meaning: The writing rules of a programming language.
terms264.example: Missing a required punctuation mark can cause a syntax error. The required marks depend on the language.

terms264.name: indentation
terms264.meaning: Spaces at the start of a line that make nesting visible. Some languages also use them to define blocks.
terms264.example: Indenting a block makes its structure easier to see; whether those spaces affect execution depends on the language.

terms264.name: parentheses
terms264.meaning: The curved marks ( and ). They group things or surround function inputs.
terms264.example: The expression (2 + 3) groups an addition inside parentheses.

terms264.name: comment
terms264.meaning: A note in code for people to read. The program does not run it as an instruction.
terms264.example: A comment can explain why a calculation rounds a result. Comment markers depend on the language.

terms264.name: output
terms264.meaning: Information a program produces or shows.
terms264.example: A greeting program can produce the output Hello.

terms264.name: input
terms264.meaning: Information given to a program or function.
terms264.example: The numbers 2 and 3 are inputs to a function that adds them.

terms264.name: bug
terms264.meaning: A mistake that makes a program behave differently from what you intended.
terms264.example: Using subtraction when you meant addition is a bug.

terms264.name: exception
terms264.meaning: A signal that something went wrong while code was running. Code may be able to handle it.
terms264.example: Trying to open a missing file can raise an exception.

terms264.name: validation
terms264.meaning: Checking that input follows the rules your program needs.
terms264.example: Before saving a score, check that it is a whole number from 0 to 100.

terms264.name: algorithm
terms264.meaning: A clear set of steps for solving a problem.
terms264.example: To find the largest number, compare each number with the largest seen so far.

terms264.name: callback
terms264.meaning: A function passed to other code so that code can call it when needed.
terms264.example: A button can call your callback when someone clicks it.

terms264.name: asynchronous
terms264.meaning: Work that can finish later, letting other work happen while you wait.
terms264.example: Loading a web page can happen while the app still responds to clicks.

terms264.name: await
terms264.meaning: Wait for an asynchronous result inside the current async function.
terms264.example: An asynchronous function can wait for requested data before using it, without blocking all unrelated work.

terms264.name: Promise
terms264.meaning: A JavaScript object for a result that may arrive later or fail.
terms264.example: A request for data can return a Promise before the data arrives.

terms264.name: state
terms264.meaning: The information an app currently remembers.
terms264.example: A counter that shows 3 has a current count state of 3.

terms264.name: event
terms264.meaning: Something that happens, such as a click, that code can respond to.
terms264.example: An input event tells your app that a field changed.

terms264.name: handler
terms264.meaning: A function that responds to an event or request.
terms264.example: A click handler can add one to a counter.

terms264.name: type
terms264.meaning: A category of value that tells code what operations make sense.
terms264.example: A number can be added. A string is text.

terms264.name: TypeScript interface
terms264.meaning: In TypeScript, a description of the properties an object should have.
terms264.example: A Player interface can require a text name and a numeric score.
terms264.context: This entry describes a TypeScript type contract. In everyday software discussion, interface can also mean a screen or a boundary between systems.

terms264.name: union type
terms264.meaning: A type that allows more than one choice.
terms264.example: string | number allows either text or a number.

terms264.name: type guard
terms264.meaning: A check that helps TypeScript narrow down what type a value has.
terms264.example: typeof value === "string" checks whether value is text.

terms264.name: generic
terms264.meaning: Code with a placeholder for a type so it can work with different types safely.
terms264.example: A collection can use a type placeholder, then accept a specific item type such as a number or text type.

terms264.name: destructure
terms264.meaning: Take named parts out of an object or array into separate names.
terms264.example: Separate the score and name from a player record into individual variables.

terms264.name: Text interpolation
terms264.meaning: Building text by inserting values from expressions. Each programming language has its own syntax for this.
terms264.example: Python: f"Hi {name}". JavaScript: `Hi ${name}`. Both insert name, but their quote marks and braces differ.
terms264.context: A JavaScript template literal and a Python f-string are related tools, not interchangeable syntax.

terms264.name: Swift protocol
terms264.meaning: In Swift, a list of requirements a type promises to provide.
terms264.example: A Transport protocol might require a description property.
terms264.context: This entry describes Swift type requirements. A network protocol instead specifies communication rules.

terms264.name: actor
terms264.meaning: In Swift, a type that helps protect its changing data when several tasks use it.
terms264.example: A store actor can keep two tasks from changing its data at the same time.

terms264.name: Swift optional
terms264.meaning: A Swift value that may contain a value or may contain nothing, written nil.
terms264.example: String? can hold "Hello" or nil.
terms264.context: This entry describes Swift’s value-or-nil type, not merely an optional task.

terms264.name: component
terms264.meaning: A reusable piece of a user interface.
terms264.example: A Profile component can show a name and picture.

terms264.name: prop
terms264.meaning: An input passed to a React component.
terms264.example: In <Profile name="Mina" />, name is a prop.

terms264.name: render
terms264.meaning: Create the description or display of what the user should see.
terms264.example: A user interface renders a heading using the current name.

terms264.name: element
terms264.meaning: A piece of a web page, often written with a start tag, content, and an end tag.
terms264.example:
Hello

is a paragraph element.

terms264.name: attribute
terms264.meaning: A named setting on an HTML element, or a named member of an object in languages such as Python.
terms264.example: In , src is an HTML attribute.

terms264.name: selector
terms264.meaning: A CSS pattern that chooses which elements to style.
terms264.example: .card chooses elements with the class card.

terms264.name: HTML/CSS class
terms264.meaning: An HTML label used to group elements, often so CSS can style them.
terms264.example: class="card" lets the CSS selector .card choose that element.
terms264.context: A reusable label on HTML elements, not an object-oriented class definition.

terms264.name: accessibility
terms264.meaning: Making an app usable by people with different needs and ways of using a computer.
terms264.example: A button should work with a keyboard as well as a mouse.

terms264.name: API
terms264.meaning: An agreed way for one piece of software to ask another for data or actions.
terms264.example: A weather app can ask a weather API for a forecast.

terms264.name: API key
terms264.meaning: A secret value that identifies or authorizes an app when it uses a service.
terms264.example: Keep an API key out of shared source code and public web pages.

terms264.name: JSON
terms264.meaning: A text format for storing or sending structured data.
terms264.example: {"name":"Mina","score":5} is JSON.

terms264.name: CSV
terms264.meaning: A text format for rows of data, often with commas between fields.
terms264.example: name,score is a header row. A later row might be Mina,5.

terms264.name: parse
terms264.meaning: Read text using rules so code can work with its structure.
terms264.example: A JSON parser can turn structured JSON text into values that code can use.

terms264.name: database
terms264.meaning: An organized place for storing and finding data.
terms264.example: A book database can store a title and author for each book.

terms264.name: SQL
terms264.meaning: A language used to work with data in relational databases.
terms264.example: SELECT title FROM books asks for book titles.

terms264.name: query
terms264.meaning: A request to find or work with data.
terms264.example: A query can ask for all books by one author.

terms264.name: row
terms264.meaning: One record in a table.
terms264.example: One row in a books table can describe one book.

terms264.name: column
terms264.meaning: One named kind of information in a table.
terms264.example: A title column holds the title for each book.

terms264.name: join
terms264.meaning: A database operation that combines matching information from tables.
terms264.example: Join orders to customers to show who placed each order.

terms264.name: SQL NULL
terms264.meaning: A marker for a missing or unknown database value.
terms264.example: NULL minutes means the minutes are unknown, not zero.
terms264.context: SQL uses three-valued logic for missing/unknown values. JavaScript null and Python None have different language rules.

terms264.name: transaction
terms264.meaning: A group of database changes handled as one unit: all succeed, or they can be undone together.
terms264.example: Moving 3 items between two counts should update both counts or neither.

terms264.name: CTE
terms264.meaning: A named query result used inside one larger SQL statement.
terms264.example: WITH totals AS (...) lets the following query use totals.

terms264.name: middleware
terms264.meaning: Code that runs as a request passes through a server, before it reaches its final handler.
terms264.example: Sign-in middleware can check who is making a request.

terms264.name: request
terms264.meaning: A message asking another program or server to do something.
terms264.example: GET /entries asks a server for saved entries.

terms264.name: response
terms264.meaning: The reply to a request.
terms264.example: A server response can contain data and a status such as 200.

terms264.name: authentication
terms264.meaning: Checking who someone is.
terms264.example: Signing in helps an app check your identity.

terms264.name: authorization
terms264.meaning: Checking what someone is allowed to do.
terms264.example: Being signed in does not mean you may edit another person’s notes.

terms264.name: terminal
terms264.meaning: A place to type commands for your computer.
terms264.example: Type a command in a terminal to build or run a local program.

terms264.name: dependency
terms264.meaning: Other code a project needs to work.
terms264.example: A project can depend on a library for reading CSV files.

terms264.name: Git
terms264.meaning: A tool that records versions of your files so you can review and recover changes.
terms264.example: A Git commit records a saved checkpoint of changes.

terms264.name: commit
terms264.meaning: In Git, a recorded checkpoint of changes with a message explaining them.
terms264.example: A commit named "Fix total" can record the corrected calculation.

terms264.name: constructor
terms264.meaning: Code used when creating an object to prepare its starting state.
terms264.example: Creating a player object can initialize its starting score.
terms264.context: Languages differ in how they allocate an object and initialize its starting state.

terms264.name: list comprehension
terms264.meaning: A short way to build a new Python list by going through other items.
terms264.example: [n * 2 for n in [1, 2]] makes [2, 4].

terms264.name: modulo
terms264.meaning: The amount left after whole-number division.
terms264.example: 7 % 3 gives 1 because 7 is two groups of 3 with 1 left.

terms264.name: module
terms264.meaning: A file or unit of code that can share its functions and values with other code.
terms264.example: A helper module can make a function available to another part of a program.

terms264.name: import
terms264.meaning: Make code from another module available here.
terms264.example: An import can make a helper function from another module available in this file.

terms264.name: finite
terms264.meaning: A finite number is not positive or negative infinity, or NaN (not a number). Those special values are called non-finite.
terms264.example: 12 is finite. Infinity and NaN are not.

terms264.name: boundary
terms264.meaning: A limit, often the smallest or largest allowed value.
terms264.example: For scores from 0 to 100, test 0 and 100 as well as numbers outside those limits.

terms264.name: timeout
terms264.meaning: A limit on how long code will wait for something.
terms264.example: A two-second timeout stops waiting if a request takes longer than two seconds.

terms264.name: retry
terms264.meaning: Try an operation again after it fails.
terms264.example: Allowing two attempts means one first try and at most one retry.

terms264.name: prerequisite
terms264.meaning: Something that must happen before another task can start.
terms264.example: Reading a file is a prerequisite for counting the words inside it.

terms264.name: cycle
terms264.meaning: A chain that leads back to something already in the chain.
terms264.example: If A needs B first and B needs A first, neither task can begin.

terms264.name: normalize
terms264.meaning: Put data into a consistent form before using it.
terms264.example: Removing extra edge spaces makes "  Read  " become "Read".

terms264.name: schema
terms264.meaning: A description of how data is organized and what kinds of values are allowed.
terms264.example: A table schema can require a name column and a numeric score column.

terms264.name: aggregate
terms264.meaning: Combine several values into one summary.
terms264.example: Adding a group of numbers produces one total.

terms264.name: reducer
terms264.meaning: A function that uses the current state and an action to decide the next state.
terms264.example: A counter reducer can turn count 3 and an add action into count 4.

terms264.name: memoized
terms264.meaning: Keeping a calculation’s previous result so it can be reused when its inputs have not changed.
terms264.example: A saved search result can be reused when the list and search text stay the same.

terms264.name: payload
terms264.meaning: The useful data carried by a message or event.
terms264.example: An event named progress might carry the payload {percent: 50}.

terms264.name: keyword
terms264.meaning: A word with a special meaning in a programming language.
terms264.example: A language can reserve words for decisions, loops or returning a result.

terms264.name: token
terms264.meaning: A small unit with meaning. In code it might be a name or symbol; in AI text it may be a word or part of one. An access token is different: it is a secret used for access.
terms264.example: In code, the name print is one token. Do not share an access token.
terms264.context: The meaning depends on context: a code token, a model’s text token, and an access token are different things. An access token may be a credential; never paste one into public examples.

terms264.name: AI
terms264.meaning: Computer systems that perform tasks such as recognizing patterns or generating text. Their answers can be wrong.
terms264.example: An AI helper may suggest code. Run and check the code before trusting it.

terms264.name: AI model
terms264.meaning: A system trained on examples to produce predictions or responses.
terms264.example: A language model can suggest an explanation, but it may invent details.
terms264.context: AI model is the broad term. A language model, including a large language model (LLM), is one kind; not every AI model generates language.

terms264.name: prompt
terms264.meaning: An instruction or question given to an AI tool. A program can also use a prompt to ask a person for input.
terms264.example: An AI prompt could be: Explain this function in two short sentences.

terms264.name: Machine learning
terms264.meaning: Building models by using data to adjust how they respond, rather than hand-writing every decision rule.
terms264.example: A message sorter learns patterns from example messages.

terms264.name: Neural network
terms264.meaning: A model built from connected calculation units, often arranged in layers. Training adjusts numerical parameters.
terms264.example: An image model combines calculations across layers to propose a label.
terms264.context: The units are mathematical operations, not living brain cells.

terms264.name: Model training
terms264.meaning: Using data and a learning method to adjust a model’s parameters or learned structure.
terms264.example: Repeated examples help adjust a model’s prediction rule.
terms264.context: Using a fact in the current conversation is not by itself a training update.

terms264.name: Inference
terms264.meaning: Using a model to calculate an output from supplied input.
terms264.example: A trained model receives a new photo and proposes a label.
terms264.context: A system can use current context during inference without changing its trained parameters.

terms264.name: Model weight
terms264.meaning: An adjustable number that controls how an input contributes to a model calculation.
terms264.example: With input 3 and weight 2, that weighted contribution is 6.
terms264.context: An attention weight calculated for the current input is distinct from a stored training parameter.

terms264.name: Loss function
terms264.meaning: A rule that measures how poorly a prediction fits the chosen training goal, using a number.
terms264.example: A distance-based loss is smaller when a numerical prediction is closer to its target.
terms264.context: Lower loss under one rule does not guarantee truth, fairness, or success on every task.

terms264.name: Backpropagation
terms264.meaning: A method that works backward through a network’s calculations to compute how parameter changes affect loss.
terms264.example: After a prediction and loss calculation, backpropagation computes gradients for the parameters.
terms264.context: Computing gradients and applying an optimizer update are separate steps.

terms264.name: Optimizer
terms264.meaning: In model training, the method that chooses parameter updates using information such as gradients.
terms264.example: An optimizer adjusts weights after gradients have been calculated.
terms264.context: This is the training meaning; software optimizers can also transform programs to improve execution.

terms264.name: Embedding
terms264.meaning: A representation of an item as a list of numbers that can capture useful relationships.
terms264.example: Words used in related contexts may have related embeddings.
terms264.context: Nearby embeddings do not prove equal meaning or factual truth.

terms264.name: Attention
terms264.meaning: A mechanism that combines information from different positions using weights calculated for the current input.
terms264.example: The words around bank can help shape its representation in river bank versus bank account.
terms264.context: Self-attention uses positions within the same sequence. It is not human awareness, and attention weights alone do not explain every answer.

terms264.name: Transformer
terms264.meaning: A neural-network design that combines attention with other transformations and information about sequence positions.
terms264.example: A text-generation Transformer can produce a continuation one token at a time.
terms264.context: Attention alone is not the complete architecture; multiple Transformer variants exist.

terms264.name: AI hallucination
terms264.meaning: A generated statement that sounds plausible but is false or unsupported.
terms264.example: An assistant invents a book title and presents it as a real source.
terms264.context: This is a description of unreliable output, not a claim that the model has a human sensory experience.

terms264.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
terms264.meaning: Finding relevant material and supplying it as context for a generated answer.
terms264.example: A support assistant retrieves a product guide before answering a setup question.
terms264.context: Retrieved material and citations still need checking; retrieval is not a guarantee of accuracy.

terms264.name: AI agent
terms264.meaning: A model-driven system that can repeatedly choose actions, use tools, inspect results, and decide what to do next.
terms264.example: An agent searches approved files, reads a result, then decides whether another search is needed.
terms264.context: The label does not guarantee autonomy or success. Permissions, stopping rules, and action receipts matter.

terms264.name: HTML
terms264.meaning: The markup language used to describe the structure and meaning of web content.
terms264.example:
Field notes

marks a main heading.

terms264.name: CSS
terms264.meaning: The language used to describe how web content is presented, including color, spacing, and layout.
terms264.example: .note { color: navy; } styles matching elements.

terms264.name: Debugging
terms264.meaning: Investigating why software behaves unexpectedly, finding the cause, and checking a correction.
terms264.example: Inspect a changing total to find where the wrong amount was added.
terms264.context: A debugger is a tool that helps inspect running code; debugging is the investigation process.

terms264.name: Refactoring
terms264.meaning: Changing the internal structure of code while keeping its intended observable behavior the same.
terms264.example: Move repeated calculations into one function, then rerun the behavior checks.

terms264.name: Technical debt
terms264.meaning: Future maintenance work caused by design or implementation choices that make later changes harder.
terms264.example: A rushed duplicated calculation must later be changed in five places.
terms264.context: A metaphor used in planning. Not every imperfection is deliberate debt, and the cost is not automatically measurable.

terms264.name: Hotfix
terms264.meaning: A focused change released urgently to correct an important problem.
terms264.example: Release a small fix for a sign-in failure before the next planned feature release.
terms264.context: Urgency does not remove the need for testing, review, and a safe rollback plan.

terms264.name: Boilerplate
terms264.meaning: Repeated setup or structural code needed before the distinctive part of a task.
terms264.example: Several small programs may share the same configuration and startup structure.
terms264.context: Common developer shorthand. Repeated code may still be necessary; do not delete it merely because it is boilerplate.

terms264.name: Rubber-duck debugging
terms264.meaning: Explaining code or a problem step by step to help notice assumptions and mistakes.
terms264.example: Describe what every line should do, then compare that with what actually happens.
terms264.context: The listener can be another person, an object, or a written explanation. They need not solve the problem for you.

terms264.name: Yak shaving
terms264.meaning: Getting drawn into a chain of supporting tasks while trying to finish an original task.
terms264.example: Before fixing one test, you find yourself updating a tool, its configuration, and its documentation.
terms264.context: Some dependencies are necessary. The phrase is a prompt to reassess scope, not proof that the work is useless.

terms264.name: Bikeshedding
terms264.meaning: Spending disproportionate discussion time on an easy minor detail while more important questions remain unresolved.
terms264.example: A team debates a button’s exact shade for an hour before deciding whether the workflow works.
terms264.context: Use carefully: a detail that seems minor to one person may matter for accessibility or another user need.

terms264.name: LGTM
terms264.meaning: A short review comment meaning the reviewer thinks the proposed change looks acceptable.
terms264.example: A teammate writes LGTM after reviewing a small change.
terms264.context: It is not proof that tests passed or formal approval unless the team’s process gives it that meaning.

terms264.name: Pull request
terms264.meaning: A proposal on a code-hosting service to review and merge a set of changes into another branch.
terms264.example: Open a pull request so teammates can inspect and discuss a bug fix.
terms264.context: Pull request and merge request are common platform-specific names for similar review workflows. Opening one does not itself merge or deploy the change.

terms264.name: integer division
terms264.meaning: Division of integer operands that discards the fractional part toward zero.
terms264.example: 11 / 3 produces 3.
terms264.context: C# and C++ foundation examples.

terms264.name: remainder operator
terms264.meaning: The % operator gives the remainder of integer division.
terms264.example: 11 % 3 produces 2.
terms264.context: C# and C++ foundation examples.

terms264.name: game state
terms264.meaning: Values describing the current game situation, such as score and turns remaining.
terms264.example: score = 0 and turns = 2 describe this game before its loop starts.
terms264.context: C# and C++ foundation examples.

terms264.name: Java class
terms264.meaning: A Java declaration that groups members such as fields and methods.
terms264.example: Our public class Main contains the main method.
terms264.context: Java 21 foundation

terms264.name: Java method
terms264.meaning: A named operation declared in a Java class or interface; it may accept parameters and return a result.
terms264.example: nextAge(8) calls a static method with argument 8.
terms264.context: Java 21 foundation

terms264.name: Java Scanner
terms264.meaning: A standard library class that reads and can convert input tokens.
terms264.example: hasNextInt checks a token before nextInt consumes it.
terms264.context: Java 21 foundation

terms264.name: Java int
terms264.meaning: A signed 32-bit whole-number primitive type.
terms264.example: int tickets = 3; declares a numeric variable.
terms264.context: Java 21 foundation

terms264.name: C function
terms264.meaning: A named operation that can receive arguments and return a result.
terms264.example: next_age(8) returns an integer value.
terms264.context: C11 foundation

terms264.name: C format string
terms264.meaning: Text directing formatted input or output; each conversion must match the corresponding argument.
terms264.example: printf("%d", boxes) displays an int.
terms264.context: C11 foundation

terms264.name: C character array
terms264.meaning: A fixed sequence of char positions; a C string stored there needs space for its zero terminator.
terms264.example: char name[6] can hold five input characters plus the string terminator.
terms264.context: C11 foundation

terms264.name: C pointer
terms264.meaning: A value identifying a location, or a null pointer value that identifies no object or function.
terms264.example: A successful fgets returns a pointer to its destination array.
terms264.context: C11 foundation

terms264.name: C header
terms264.meaning: A file included to provide declarations and other preprocessing information.
terms264.example: stdio.h declares standard input/output functions.
terms264.context: C11 foundation

terms264.name: Java boolean
terms264.meaning: A primitive type with exactly the values true and false.
terms264.example: seats >= 2 produces a boolean result.
terms264.context: Java 21 foundation

terms264.name: C comparison result
terms264.meaning: For the relational and equality comparisons here, int 1 means true and int 0 means false.
terms264.example: seats >= 2 can select an if branch.
terms264.context: C11 foundation
